name: Compact nodules
prompt:
Use case: style-transfer. Asset type: transparent pixel-art ore-outcrop sprite atlas for the existing strategy game.
Transform the supplied mountain atlas into an ore-outcrop atlas. Input image 1 is the approved mountain artwork: preserve its angular cream-lit upper-left rock planes, broad mid-gray facets, dark lower-right faces, olive ground contact, stepped pixel silhouette, and restrained palette. Input image 2 is the actual game terrain at native 16px cells: use it to match camera, scale, and pixel density only. Change the landforms to SMALL exposed mineral-bearing fragments of those same mountains, intended to sit on clear flat ground directly alongside the foot of a grassy hill or mountain. No tall mountains in the output.
One precisely aligned 3-column by 2-row sprite sheet, SIX complete isolated objects. Transparent background, generous clear gutters, no ground tiles or panels, no painted checkerboard. Columns from left to right: COPPER, IRON, GOLD. Row 1 uses one asymmetrical rock silhouette repeated across the three materials; row 2 uses a second different silhouette repeated across the materials.
Copper: restrained rust-orange/coral mineral flecks with occasional oxidized turquoise dots embedded flush in gray rock. Iron: distinctly cool slate-blue/steel-blue flecks with pale silver facets embedded flush in gray rock. Gold: rich ochre-yellow flecks and short gold seams, a few pale yellow lit pixels, embedded flush in the same gray rock. Keep gray/cream host rock dominant, about 75–85 percent, mineral flecks 15–25 percent. Flecks must be readable at actual game scale, clustered into a few clear angular patches and small broken seams. No loose coins, no gems, no large crystals, no glow, no outlines around each mineral bit, no mine doors, no equipment, no text or labels, no buildings, no people. Fixed top-down oblique game camera and upper-left light; do not rotate or mirror. All artwork is hard-edged low-resolution pixel clusters, enlarged nearest-neighbor, without brush texture, gradients, blur, antialiasing, noise, or tiny decorative detail.

OPTION 1: Very chunky, slightly cartoon-like one-cell outcrops, designed to read at 16x16 native pixels. Each rock uses 3–4 strong rock planes, one low angular knuckle with a smaller attached toe, around 14 logical pixels across and 10 high. Broad heavy silhouette; sparse but bold mineral flecks, each 1–2 logical pixels. Stay low enough to clearly read as exposed ore-bearing boulders, not little pyramidal mountains. Row 2 is a flatter twin-knuckle version. Render crisp visibly coarse logical pixels; each sprite is a uniformly enlarged 16x16 design. Preserve generous transparency around the shape.
